title: [ty] Propagate outer type context through cast calls
body:
On `main`, the first call to `f()` here succeeds without error due to the type context supplied by the annotation of the `x` parameter. The second call to `f()`, however, causes us to emit `disjoint-cast`: `["foo"]` is inferred as having type `list[str]`, since the intermediate `cast()` call means the type context of the `f` parameter is not propagated through, and `list[str]` is disjoint from `list[Literal["foo"]]`.

```python
from typing import Literal, cast

def f(x: list[Literal["foo"]]): ...

f(["foo"])
f(cast(list[Literal["foo"]], ["foo"]))
```

This PR changes our behaviour so that we propagate type context through `cast()` calls. With this change, the second argument to the `cast()` call is inferred as `list[Literal["foo"]]` due to the outer type context, and instead of emitting `disjoint-cast` we emit `redundant-cast`, reflecting the fact that `["foo"]` would be inferred as having exactly the same inferred type without the cast.

The propagated context is treated as an inference hint. We speculatively infer the value with that context and retain the result if it produces no diagnostics other than `redundant-cast`. Otherwise, we discard the attempt and infer the value with its original context. Only the chosen attempt's types and diagnostics are retained.

The fallback avoids introducing errors in expressions whose types the cast is intended to override. For example, propagating the return annotation here would infer the lambda parameter as `int` and report `call-non-callable`:

```python
from typing import Callable, cast

def callback() -> Callable[[int], str]:
    return cast(Callable[[int], str], lambda value: value())  # no diagnostic
```

Retrying without the outer context leaves the lambda parameter's type unknown. Diagnostics that also occur without the propagated context are still reported. The implementation shares the existing collection peer-context fallback mechanism and caches nested expressions to avoid exponential inference work when retrying.

## Rejected alternatives

An alternative strategy here would be to use the target type of the `cast()` call _itself_ as type context for the second argument to `cast()`, rather than simply propagating outer type context through the `cast()` call. I tried this in https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28847. However, I don't think that approach would give us the appropriate semantics. If we did this, we would report `redundant-cast` for situations like the following, since we would use the first argument to the `cast()` call (`list[object]`) as context for inferring `[42]`.

```py
from typing import cast

for x in cast(list[object], [42]):  # redundant-cast
    reveal_type(x)
```

But the `cast()` call here is not redundant: if it were removed, `[42]` would be inferred as `list[Literal[42]]` instead of `list[object]`, and `x` would be inferred as `Literal[42]` instead of `object`, changing the inferred types later on in the program.
